 Judgment

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 07.07.2020 passed in MVC No.243/2008 by the III Additional District and Sessions Judge, Tumakuru (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
That on 05.12.2017 at about 7.00 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding in his two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-06 EP 5128 on Anthapura - Chelurhatti Road and when he reached near Doddamma's Mangalore Garden land, Chellurhatti, Chelur Hobli, Gubbi Taluk, at that time a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-06 EW 7925, which is duly insured with the second respondent - Insurance Company and being driven in a rash and negligent manner, came and dashed against the two wheeler of the petitioner, because of which, the petitioner has sustained the following injuries:-
"(i) Pecuniary damages (Special damages).
(ii) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, maintenance, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
(II) Loss of earnings and other gains which the injured would have made at he has not been injured comprising loss of earnings during the period of treatment.
(a) Loss of earnings during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.

(c) Future medical expenditure (non-pecuniary damages and general damages).
(d) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as consequence of the injuries.
(e) Loss of amenities or lass of prospects of marriage.
(f) Loss of expectation of life or loss of normal longitivity.
4. The Tribunal, based on the evidence let in, has awarded a compensation of Rs.1,93,000/- along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
5. The petitioner to prove his case has examined himself as PW-1.
He has not examined any Doctor and has not been able to prove any permanent body disability due to the accident.
However, he has been able to establish the nature of injuries suffered by him and the Insurance Company does not dispute the same.

Hence, the Tribunal has awarded the aforementioned compensation of Rs.1,93,000/- to the petitioner under the following heads:-
Heads of compensation awarded:
01.
Towards medical expense Rs. 1,34,000-00 Loss of income during 02. Rs. 9,000-00 treatment period 03. Pain and suffering Rs. 20,000-00 04. Loss of amenities Rs. 20,000-00 Conveyance & attendant 05.
Rs. 10,000-00 charges

The petitioner contends that even though he has not examined the Doctor and has not been able to establish the permanent physical disability due to the accident, given the nature of injuries, the Tribunal ought to have granted higher compensation to him.
7. The learned counsel for the second respondent - Insurance Company justifies the order passed by the Tribunal and prays for dismissal of the appeal.
8. Based on actual bills submitted by the petitioner, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,34,000/- towards 'medical expenses' and I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards 'loss of income during treatment period', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.9,000/-.
Admittedly, the accident happened in the year 2017.
The petitioner has not established his income before the Tribunal.
However, the nature of injuries is not in dispute.

Based on the injuries sustained atleast 3 S S Siddananjappa vs Nagaraju on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181721822/
3 months has to be considered as laid up period and the income of the petitioner which needs to be fixed notionally in the absence of proof of income, has to be considered at Rs.11,000/- per month as per the Lok Adalath chart.

Hence, under this head the compensation is enhanced to Rs.33,000/-
(11,000x3=33,000).
Towards 'pain and suffering', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-.
Given the nature of injuries, as there are three fractures, I deem it appropriate to enhance the compensation to Rs.60,000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities' the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-.
Given the nature of injuries, I am of the opinion it is appropriate to enhance it to Rs.50,000/-.
Towards 'conveyance and attendant charges' the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- based on the evidence let-in.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
9. Thus, the compensation to the petitioner under different heads are modified as hereunder:-

 Towards medical  1 1,34,000-00 1,34,000-00  expenses  Loss of income during  2 9,000-00 33,000-00  treatment period  3 Pain and suffering 20,000-00 60,000-00
4 Loss
of amenities
20,000-00 50,000-00  Conveyance & attendant

Thus, the petitioner would be entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.94,000/- (Rs.2,87,000/-
minus Rs.1,93,000/-) over and above what has been already awarded by the Tribunal.

Further given the bank rate of interest, I deem it appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition before the Tribunal till realization.
Hence, the following:-
The said sum shall be paid to the petitioner by respondent No.2- Insurance Company within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of the judgment and order.
iii) Draw modified award accordingly.
